source.citation: Radtke-Schuller S, Schuller G, Angenstein F, Grosser OS, Goldschmidt J, Budinger E (2016). Brain atlas of the Mongolian gerbil (Meriones unguiculatus) in CT/MRI-aided stereotaxic coordinates. Brain Struct Funct 221(Suppl 1):1-272.
source.note: Structure/plate assignments taken verbatim from the authors' published Index of structures. Plate AP coordinates derived from the linear stereotaxic series printed on each plate (bregma 7.80 mm at plate 1, 350 um steps) and verified by OCR of all 62 plates.

conventions.plane: coronal (frontal), perpendicular to the brainstem axis
conventions.ap_zero: bregma (also given for lambda, interaural line, occipital crest)
conventions.ap_sign: positive = anterior to the landmark; plate 1 is the most anterior
conventions.dv_zero: plane through the most dorsal points of cerebrum and cerebellum; negative is ventral

plate_frame.note: Converts a position on a frame-cropped plate image into stereotaxic millimeters. The images are cropped to the atlas's own printed coordinate box rather than to fixed page fractions, so this one calibration holds for all 62 plates. AP comes from the plate's bregma; together the three give a full stereotaxic triplet for every entry in label_positions.
plate_frame.derivation: Least-squares fit of the 1 mm tick lattice the atlas prints in its own coordinate box, read from all 62 plates: ML ticks -8 to +8 mm in the bottom border (rows 683-691), DV ticks +1 to -10 mm in the right border (columns 1022-1031), thresholded at gray < 140. Across the 62 plates the fits agree to 56.999 +/- 0.007 px/mm about x = 519.99 +/- 0.05 for ML, and 56.798 +/- 0.007 px/mm about y = 95.81 +/- 0.11 for DV; the largest single-tick residual on any plate is 0.42 px.
plate_frame.validation: Checked against anatomy, not just the fit. Midline structures sit within 0.10 mm of ML 0 (3V -0.02, Aq -0.04, 4V +0.01, cc +0.03, MnR -0.04 mm mean), and bilateral pairs are symmetric at the published widths (MSO +/-1.33, LSO +/-1.67, Au1 +/-6.48 mm). All 6,266 labels fall between DV -9.02 and -0.52 mm, i.e. below the dorsal surface plane, as they must.

mri_frame.note: Converts a voxel of the atlas's own MRI into stereotaxic millimeters. The volume is already in the atlas frame, one slice per plate, so nothing here is fitted along AP: plate = 62 - slice. The first six keys are the ones atlaslib.Frame reads.
mri_frame.plate_of_slice: 62 - slice; slices 62-71 lie rostral of plate 1
mri_frame.derivation: ml_px_per_mm and dv_px_per_mm are the TIFF's own XResolution (217.094 pixels per inch, i.e. 0.117 mm/px), read off the file and checked on load rather than fitted. ap_step is the one number the file does not carry - there is no ImageDescription and no z tag - and was recovered: it is conventions.spacing_mm, the atlas's own plate spacing, and plate_of_slice then falls out identically rather than being fitted. ml_zero_px is the column minimising the left-right mirror difference over the cerebral slices; dv_zero_px is the atlas's DV zero, fitted by maximising the image gradient under the brain_outline rings.
mri_frame.validation: Projecting brain_outline onto the MRI under this map, with no AP fitting at all, leaves no systematic bias in either in-plane axis: over all 62 plates the median best whole-pixel shift is 0.000 mm in both DV and ML, with a per-plate scatter of about 0.39 mm and 0.38 mm, i.e. three voxels (build_mri.py --verify). Three further checks agree and none was fitted for: slice 0 lands on plate 62 and slice 61 on plate 1, consuming the 62 plates exactly with nothing left over; slice 18, the only slice in the stack carrying a burned-in mark, is bregma -7.25, which is the atlas's interaural AP zero (plate 44); and in a mid-sagittal reformat the dorsal cortical surface sits at DV 0, which is the atlas's own definition of DV zero. The residual worth knowing about is a small yaw: the per-slice mirror-symmetry column drifts across the series, so a single ml_zero_px carries a systematic ML error of a few tenths of a millimeter at the ends.

residual.note: Whole-pixel shift per plate that best lines brain_outline up with the image gradient, in millimeters. Written by build_mri.py --verify.

groups.note: Gross divisions of the brain, added here and not part of the published atlas. Each is a named union of the atlas's own structures; groups may overlap. A group is only on the plates listed, which for the pons and the medulla is narrower than where their members reach. Built by tools/build_groups.py.
groups.pons_medulla_boundary: the caudal end of the facial nucleus, plate 49

data.name: cerebral cortex
data.note: Isocortex, the cingulate and retrosplenial belt, the insular and orbital fields, the rhinal cortices, piriform cortex, the cortical layers the atlas names separately, and the claustro-endopiriform complex. The dorsal and external cortices of the inferior colliculus carry the atlas's `cortex` tag and are not cerebral cortex; they are filed under midbrain alone.

data.name: hippocampal formation
data.note: The atlas's hippocampal tag: the CA fields and their layers, the dentate gyrus, the subicular complex, entorhinal cortex, and the fiber systems the formation is defined by (fornix, fimbria, alveus, the hippocampal commissures).

data.name: olfactory areas
data.note: The main and accessory olfactory bulbs, the anterior olfactory nucleus, tenia tecta, piriform cortex, the endopiriform nuclei, the olfactory tubercle and islands of Calleja, and the lateral olfactory tract.

data.name: olfactory bulb
data.note: The bulb proper: every layer of the main and accessory olfactory bulbs, the olfactory nerve layer, the intrabulbar anterior commissure and the olfactory ventricle. A subset of olfactory areas.

data.name: amygdala
data.note: The amygdaloid complex, including its cortical nuclei and the amygdalohippocampal and amygdalopiriform transition areas.

data.name: striatum and pallidum
data.note: Dorsal and ventral striatum (caudate putamen, accumbens, olfactory tubercle, islands of Calleja), the pallidum (globus pallidus, ventral pallidum, entopeduncular nucleus) and the subthalamic nucleus.

data.name: septum and basal forebrain
data.note: The septal nuclei, the diagonal band and magnocellular basal forebrain, substantia innominata, and the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis with its stria. The ventral striatum and pallidum are filed under striatum and pallidum instead, though the atlas tags them here.

data.name: thalamus
data.note: Dorsal thalamus, the geniculate bodies, the reticular and midline nuclei, the epithalamus and zona incerta. The atlas tags many hypothalamic nuclei `thalamus` as well; those are excluded here.

data.name: hypothalamus
data.note: The hypothalamic nuclei and areas, the mammillary bodies, the median eminence and the hypothalamic tracts.

data.name: midbrain
data.note: Tectum (superior and inferior colliculi), the pretectum, the periaqueductal gray, the tegmentum, substantia nigra and the ventral tegmental area, the red nucleus and the oculomotor and trochlear nuclei. The dorsal raphe is here where the atlas prints it rostral of the pontine nuclei; its caudal subdivisions fall at pontine levels and are filed there.

data.name: pons
data.note: From the first plate that prints the pontine nuclei to the last that prints the facial nucleus (plates 39–49, bregma −5.50 to −9.00 mm): the basis pontis and pontine tegmentum, the superior olivary complex and the nuclei of the lateral lemniscus, the parabrachial nuclei, the trigeminal motor and principal sensory nuclei, and the facial and abducens nuclei.

data.name: medulla
data.note: Caudal to the facial nucleus (plates 50–62, bregma −9.35 to −13.55 mm): the medullary reticular formation and raphe, the inferior olive, the solitary and spinal trigeminal complexes, the dorsal column nuclei, the vestibular and cochlear nuclei, and the caudal cranial nerve nuclei.

data.name: brainstem
data.note: Midbrain, pons and medulla together — exactly the union of those three, so anything in one of them is in this.

data.name: cerebellum
data.note: The cerebellar cortex lobules, the deep nuclei, the peduncles and the cerebellar fissures.

data.name: fiber tracts
data.note: Every named tract, commissure, lemniscus, fascicle and cranial nerve root. These run through the gray-matter divisions rather than beside them, so most are in one of those as well.

data.name: ventricular system
data.note: The ventricles and their recesses, the aqueduct and central canal, the choroid plexus and ependyma, and the circumventricular organs. The periaqueductal gray is filed under midbrain, though the atlas tags it here.

data.name: frontal cortex
data.note: Motor, orbital, prelimbic, infralimbic and cingulate fields. A subset of cerebral cortex.

data.name: parietal cortex
data.note: Primary and secondary somatosensory fields and the parietal association areas. A subset of cerebral cortex.

data.name: temporal cortex
data.note: The auditory fields, temporal association cortex, and the ectorhinal and perirhinal belt. A subset of cerebral cortex.

data.name: occipital cortex
data.note: Primary and secondary visual fields. A subset of cerebral cortex.

features.note: The abbreviations the atlas prints that name no region: the fissures and sulci, which are the clefts between regions and are drawn as the lines between them; `cbw`, which is the white matter core of whichever lobule it runs through and not a lobule of its own; and the vessels, which are not brain. `kinds` gives the sentence each is read by. These are named, indexed, searchable and located exactly as every other structure is, and every place a plate prints one is in `label_positions`; what they have no claim on is area, so build_region_extents.py does not seed them, they hold no entry in `region_extents`, and they have no volume or mesh. The ground they used to be given goes to the regions the atlas does draw a boundary for -- a lobule now reaches across the white matter that splits it, as the drawing has it. `hif` and `dcw` are not here: the hippocampal fissure is a space the atlas draws a boundary round, and the deep cerebral white matter is a territory of its own rather than a name printed inside another structure.

kinds.fissure: a cleft between regions, not a region
kinds.sulcus: a groove between regions, not a region
kinds.incisure: a notch in the surface, not a region
kinds.white matter: the white matter of the lobules it runs through, not a lobule of its own
kinds.vessel: a vessel on the section, not part of the brain

verification.method: Labels were read in two passes. Pass 1 rendered every plate at 300 dpi, isolated the black label text by color and OCR'd it with Tesseract. Pass 2 re-read all 62 plates from the lossless 300 dpi PNGs embedded in the source PDF, using a recognizer built for this typeface: 11,985 labeled glyph exemplars harvested from the pass-1 labels, matched as baseline-anchored binary templates (99.75% top-3 per character under leave-one-plate-out validation), then whole tokens parsed against the 723 published abbreviations by Viterbi segmentation. Where two abbreviations are visually identical in this font (Gl/GI, IPl/IPI, GlA/GiA) the published plate ranges break the tie: those pairs never overlap.
verification.note: 3339 of 3510 index entries now carry at least one located label (95.1%, up from 2532), from 6322 individual printed labels (up from 4164). The index lists 3510 rather than 3506 pairs because four structures whose printed range is malformed are read as spanning one plate more; see index_range_corrections. A third pass added the last 37 of those, over 23 entries: where the index lists a structure for a plate and no label was located, the word was cut from a plate that does carry it and matched back by normalized cross-correlation, and every candidate was read against the printed page before being kept (tools/find_missing_labels.py). Pass 2 re-found 96.7% of the pass-1 labels and added 2073 more, including second-hemisphere labels that pass 1 caught on one side only (for example Au1 on plate 33). Every reading that disagreed with the existing record, fell below the confidence floor, or named a structure the index does not list for that plate was inspected on the plate image; 17 pass-1 records were superseded by the printed text (Cl->DCl, Su3->Su3C, PR->PrC, ml->mlf, Rh->PRh, La->LaV, A1->A11, V1->V2L, cg->Cg1, f->fr, ts->rs and layer digits read as S1/AI). A fourth pass ran the same matcher again, which is not idempotent: every label it writes becomes a template for the next run, so words invisible to one pass can be unambiguous to the next. It added 9 labels over 5 pairs -- the four newly in range (AngT 29, ZIC 35, Su3C 37, RLi 36) and mlf on plate 44, which is the only plate between 38 and 55 the abbreviation was missing from -- and a further pass over the result found nothing more. A fifth pass took the twenty structures no plate carried a located copy of, which the third and fourth could not reach at all: those passes cut the word out of a plate that carries it, and for these there was none to cut. Their words were composed instead, letter by letter, from glyphs cut out of located labels on neighboring plates -- the face sets its letters with clear white between, so a located word is a row of letters already read -- and matched by the same cross-correlation, with every candidate put beside the printed page and read before it was kept (tools/find_unlettered.py). It added 26 labels over 19 pairs, and settled nine of the twenty in full: AVPe, Bo, DTgP, MnA, PSol, RPO, SChVM, dcs and tfp, with SolC on four of its eight plates. The eleven left are not a shortfall of the search but of the premise, because ten of them are not printed as their own word anywhere: 9aCb and 9bCb share one label set `9a,bCb`; 9N is inside `9/11N`; SolC on plates 56-59, and SolM, SolDL, SolV and SolVL throughout, are lettered by bare suffix -- `M`, `DL`, `V`, `VL`, `C` -- around a single `sol`; and p1PAG and p1Rt are set in italic, the only italics on any plate, so no exemplar of that face exists to compose from. A sixth pass then took the first of those cases at its word. `9a,bCb` is not a word the reader failed on; it is two words the atlas says once, eliding the `9` they share and the `Cb` they share, and the same convention gives `9/11N` and `3/4Cb`. label_blocks reads the joins the atlas makes *between* two labels; a mark *inside* one token goes past it, because the reader sees one run of ink and either takes the longest abbreviation that fits -- `9/11N` reads as `11N`, so 9N is never located -- or fails on the whole run. So every ordered pair the index lists on a plate with one of them unlocated was elided that way, composed, and matched (tools/find_compounds.py). The mark is left blank in the template, there being no comma anywhere inside the 723 abbreviations to compose one from, and is then tested for separately: ink standing in that gap is what tells a real elision from a word with a stray letter beside it, and ink lying on a path traced in svg/ is a drawn boundary rather than a mark. All 146 candidates over 116 tokens were read against the printed page -- the highest-scoring of them, at 0.88, is two separate labels on plate 39 -- and six tokens are real: `9a,bCb` on all eight of its plates, `9/11N`, `3/4Cb`, `InG/Wh`, `RSGb/c` and `S1J/BF`. Each member holds the whole token's box and the pair is a group in label_blocks, as the bracketed joins already were, so the region pass seeds them as one. That settles 9aCb, 9bCb and 9N, which no amount of searching for them as words could have, and closes a plate each for S1BF, RSGc, InWh and 3Cb. Of the eleven, Y is the last that is printed as its own word: a capital that appears in no other abbreviation in the index, so there is no letter to build it out of. Two changes were then made by hand. The left-hemisphere `PtP` on plate 30, which none of the passes could see -- they look for a name with no location on a plate, not for one missing its second instance -- was found by cutting the located instance as a template and matching it across the page (0.927), and read against the print before it was kept. And the eight second boxes the sixth pass had left on members it was anchored on -- a member already located from the same ink kept its own box and took the token's as well -- were removed, with the loose pass-1 box `GrA` on plate 8 carried beside its tight one, so that a printed word is one label. A seventh pass took seven more by hand, all of them second instances of a word already located on the same plate, which no pass looks for: `1` four times on plate 17 and twice on plate 18 -- the cortical layer digits, printed once per hemisphere beside Pir and again beside Tu -- and `OV` on plate 5, the right-hand half of the label `E/OV`. A bare `1` cannot be found by matching the word alone: it scores 0.98 against the 1 inside S1DZ, M1 and Cg1 and against the coordinate ticks, so the match was restricted to the neighbourhood of a `2` or `3` the pass had read, the digits being printed as a stack, and every candidate was read against the printed page. Two candidates that scored well were rejected there: the I of ICj on plate 17 and the i of Pir on plate 18. Of the older shortfall, what remains is still expected: a structure listed for a plate range is not necessarily labeled on every plate of that range.

index_range_corrections.note: The published index writes a bare plate number for a structure that appears on one plate (104 of them) and a range for a structure that appears on several. Seven entries are written with a dash and no second plate to go with it, and the Index of structures is the only place this shows: the Index of abbreviations renders three of them as a plain number. Four are set as N-N. All four have the abbreviation printed on plate N+1 as well, read against the plate image, so the dash is taken at its word and the range is read as N to N+1. The other three (CAT 43-, IVF 25-, MnM 34-) have nothing printed past the plate they list -- every candidate over 0.55 on the following plates turned out to be a different word (VEn, VP, MoDG) -- and are left at the single plate. This is the one place the database departs from the printed index; tools/check_indexes.py reproduces the comparison.

verification.coordinates: Plate AP coordinates were OCR'd from all 62 plates and matched the analytic series (bregma 7.80 mm at plate 1, -0.35 mm per plate; lambda = bregma+4.45; interaural = bregma+7.25; occipital crest = bregma+9.95) exactly, with one OCR sign error on plate 34 corrected against the model.
verification.plate_registration: Plates were cropped relative to the printed coordinate frame, detected per page, rather than to fixed page fractions. In the source PDF the plate 31 figure sits 118 px (300 dpi) lower on the page than every other plate, and plates 1 and 10 are offset by 2-3 px; frame-relative cropping removes these offsets so all 62 plate images share one coordinate frame.
verification.off_index_labels: label_positions holds only structure-plate pairs the published index lists, so the printed labels above are recorded here rather than in label_positions.

brain_outline.note: Outline of the section on each plate: what a track has to cross to reach a target, and the surface a depth is measured from. Keyed by plate; each entry is a list of closed polygons, and each polygon a list of [x, y] fractions of the frame-cropped plate image, read with the same two formulae as label_positions. Most plates give one polygon. Some give more, and anatomically so: the interhemispheric fissure splits plates 10-14 in two, the cortex parts from the midbrain on plates 37-42, and the cerebellum from the brainstem on plates 56-59; and two structures stand clear of the section altogether, the optic chiasm on plate 22 and the mammillary body on plate 36.
brain_outline.derivation: Taken from the labeled drawings by the same steps the 3-D view already runs in v3build(): crop to [14, 14, 1020, 681] of the 1100x703 frame, call a pixel ink where its smallest channel is below 236, flood the paper in from the border, and keep the connected components of what the paper did not reach that are larger than max(400 px scaled to full resolution, 2% of the largest). Two components are kept that the rule drops, which over the 62 plates is every one of them carrying a printed name. On plate 36 the atlas draws the mammillary body clear of the rest of the section, and at 1,628 px against a 2% floor of 5,131 it was culled, taking ML -- printed inside it -- with it. On plate 22 it draws the optic chiasm the same way, and at 3,515 px against a floor of 4,331 that was culled too, taking och: the structure came out with a hole at plate 22 in a run the published index gives as 21-25. Both islands are far over the 400 px floor and were dropped only for being small beside a whole section, and a face outside the outline can never be named -- build_region_extents.py fills the outline for the section interior. Both are traced by the same steps and kept as their plate's second polygon. Holes are filled, so a ventricle counts as brain. The boundary of each surviving component is then traced and simplified by Douglas-Peucker at 2 px (35 um), which is well inside the atlas's own error. No morphological opening: one large enough to take off the leader lines the drawing points at labels outside the section also eats the thin cortical sheet on plates 36 and 38, which is real. The contour therefore runs a few pixels out along a leader line here and there, and a reader should take the first crossing that is followed by a fifth of a millimeter of brain rather than the first crossing outright.
brain_outline.validation: Three checks, none of which the extraction was tuned to pass. The atlas puts DV 0 at the plane through the most dorsal points of cerebrum and cerebellum, and the highest point of any outline on any plate is DV -0.06 mm - the surface reaches that plane and does not cross it. The lowest is DV -9.09 mm, and the deepest of the 6,322 printed labels sits at DV -9.02, just inside it. And 97.8% of those labels fall inside the outline of their own plate; of the 139 that do not, the largest group is on the olfactory bulb plates 5-9, where the drawing prints the label outside the section and points at it, and the median one is 0.12 mm out.

label_positions.note: Screen positions of the printed abbreviation labels on each plate. Keyed by plate, then abbreviation; each entry is a list of [cx, cy, w, h] fractions of the frame-cropped plate image (labels usually appear twice, once per hemisphere, and layered structures such as cerebellar white matter many more times). Multiply by width_px/height_px in plate_frame and apply its formulae to read a label's position as stereotaxic ML and DV in millimeters.

label_blocks.note: Abbreviations the atlas typesets into one printed label, per plate, and so names of one region between them rather than of one each: "S1Tr/ LPtA", "Au1 (A1)", "Au1 (A1/AAF)". Read off the printed page by tools/label_blocks.py, from the punctuation that joins them -- a slash between two names or ending the line above, or a bracket around the line below. Order is as printed, so the first is the name the label leads with. region_extents seeds a group as one, and the app answers for any name in a group with the group's one outline.

region_extents.note: Area of each structure on each plate, as a list of closed polygons of [x, y] fractions of the frame-cropped plate image, the same frame and convention brain_outline uses. `s` is the share of that polygon's border that lies on ink the tracing actually drew, one entry per polygon; `a` is the entry's area in mm2 on that plate; `n` is how many printed abbreviations seeded it. A polygon with a high `s` is the boundary the atlas printed. A low one is a split the extraction had to infer because the drawing does not separate those structures, and should be read as an estimate. `w`, where it is present, says the entry has no outline of its own on this plate: every one of its seeds fell inside a boundary the atlas draws around more than one name and prints nothing within, and most of the border stored here is that split rather than ink. The cerebellar lobules are the largest of them; the mediodorsal thalamus and the lateral hypothalamic zones are most of the rest. Read the geometry of a `w` entry as the extraction's best guess at where one name gives way to the next, and not as a boundary to show anyone. Abbreviations the atlas typesets into one label -- see `label_blocks` -- share one entry, filed under the name the label leads with, because they name one region between them. The names that are no region -- see `features` -- have no entry here at all: a fissure is the line between two regions rather than a region, so the ground either side of it belongs to the regions it separates, and that is where it is filed.
region_extents.derivation: Built by tools/build_region_extents.py from the traced outlines in svg/ and the located abbreviations in label_positions. The traced paths are bridged across their dangling ends, closed against brain_outline, and cut into faces; a face sealed by traced ink and holding one abbreviation is that structure's area as drawn. Faces holding several abbreviations are split by a watershed seeded on the printed labels and ridged on the distance transform of the ink. Abbreviations the atlas typesets into one printed label are seeded as one rather than against each other. An abbreviation the atlas prints on one hemisphere only is mirrored about ML 0 into the other, and the mirror kept where it lands in a face the drawing seals and no printed abbreviation names, and where more than half of that face reflects into the faces the mirrors came from; what is printed in a face always wins, so nothing here renames anything. Faces still holding no label are left unassigned rather than absorbed. The abbreviations `features` lists are located as every label is and then not seeded: they name a cleft, a white matter core or a vessel rather than a territory, and a face lettered only with one of them is left in play for the regions around it to flood rather than made a hole. Polygons are simplified by Douglas-Peucker at 2 px, as brain_outline is. See METHODS.md.
region_extents.validation: 3067 structure-plate entries carry an area -- 96% of the 3,204 the label pass located, 91% of the 3,365 the published index lists, both counted over the structures that are regions -- as 5881 polygons over 166844 points. Of the 6321 printed labels seeded, 233 are printed outside their region with a line drawn back into it and were seeded at the end of that line rather than on the word -- see `label_leaders`. A further 192 sat on a boundary, or on a line this pass could not follow, and were pulled to the largest face within a millimeter; 1 could not be resolved at all. 124 more seeds are not printed labels at all but mirrors of one about ML 0, filling a face the drawing seals on the hemisphere the atlas did not letter. 297 of the seeds name no region at all -- the 20 fissures, sulci, vessels and the cerebellar white matter that `features` lists -- and the 176 mm2 they were holding is given back at the end of the pass, each pixel of it to whichever region is nearest around the ink the atlas drew. They are seeded and then emptied rather than left out, because a seed in the depth of the white matter is what stops the lobules racing each other down it; what it must not do is keep the ground, which is the lobule's. It is why `Crus2` is its whole lobule here rather than a wedge of it. 294 entries carry `w`: they sit only inside boundaries the atlas draws around more than one name and prints nothing within, and most of the border stored for them is the split rather than the ink. Three checks, none of which the extraction was tuned to pass. (1) Every boundary between two regions is stored as one polyline, twice: 100% of directed boundary edges have their reverse in exactly one neighbor, so the regions tile the section without overlapping it or leaving a sliver. (2) 98% of printed labels fall inside the region they name, read at the end of the line where the atlas draws one. (3) Regions plus unassigned faces account for the section area to within 2% on the worst plate. Per polygon, the share of the border lying on ink the tracing actually drew: median 1.00, 81% at or above 0.90, 90% at or above 0.75, 3% below 0.50.

region_colors.note: The palette slot every region wears, on every plate it is drawn on. Solved once over all 62 plates together, because a color that holds across the atlas cannot be found one plate at a time. No two regions that touch -- share a point, or come within 0.05 mm of one another -- are given the same slot, and beyond that a slot means nothing at all. The palette itself is the app's. Built by tools/build_region_colors.py.
region_colors.derivation: Two regions touch on a plate when they share a vertex of the extents or their boundaries come within 0.05 mm. Every such pair over the 62 plates is an edge, except a pair with no printed boundary between it on any plate where it touches at all, which is a merge instead -- taken in order and refused where it would put a printed boundary inside one patch. The patches are then colored with 8 slots: the k-core by tabu search from a DSATUR start, seeded so the run reproduces, and the peeled remainder in the reverse of the order it came off. 8 is the fewest that can work, because 1, 2, 3, AHA, ICj, Pir, Tu, VP pairwise touch.
region_colors.validation: Every one of the 688 regions the atlas draws carries one slot, held on every plate it appears on. The 688 regions make 631 patches, joined on 74 of the 189 pairs the atlas prints no boundary between; 28 joins were refused because a printed boundary ran inside the patch they would have made. 87 pairs are drawn open on one plate and split by a printed line on another, and the printed line decides those. No two regions that touch wear the same slot on any plate. 8 slots are used over the atlas and at most 8 on one plate; 8 is the fewest possible, since 1, 2, 3, AHA, ICj, Pir, Tu, VP all touch one another.

label_leaders.note: Where the atlas prints an abbreviation outside the region it names and draws a line to it, this is the far end of that line: the position the label means, as [i, x, y], where i indexes that abbreviation's list in label_positions on the same plate and x, y are fractions of the frame-cropped plate image, the frame plate_frame calibrates. The box in label_positions is still where the word is printed and is still what a reader hovers; this is where it points. Where the atlas typesets several names as one label -- see label_blocks -- the one line it draws is recorded against every name in it, because it is drawn from the whole label. Labels without a line are absent: for those the box is the position.

plate_registration.note: The affine [a, b, c, d, e, f] that maps the traced page (3296 x 2481 px; 2481 x 3296 for plate 20) into the 1100 x 703 plate frame: x' = a x + c y + e, y' = b x + d y + f. Fitted per plate against the plate's own printed ink (METHODS.md, Vectorized outlines). The same matrices sit beside the traced paths in data/vec.json.

version.note: version is the release of this repository the data belongs to; generated is the day the derived fields were last recomputed by tools/export_tables.py.
